newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr takes breather, steady vs yen by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr takes breather, steady vs yen by late Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar steadied against the yen by late afternoon Tokyo on Tuesday after earlier gains were trimmed by sales from U.S. operators and interbank traders, dealers said. They said constant short-covering interest helped support the dollar on the downside.
The market took a breather after recent wild fluctuations, and little impact was seen from comments by Japanese officials.
In late trade, some traders bought back the dollar for yen, partly in reaction to weaker-than-expected economic data, which pushed JGB yields lower.
The yield of the key 10-year 182nd JGB stood at 2.500 percent at 0632 GMT, down from the 2.590 percent Monday close.

Japan's private-sector machinery orders, excluding those for machinery at electric power firms and for ships, fell a seasonally adjusted 12.7 percent in March from the previous month to 1.02 trillion yen.
Dealers said the dollar remained top-heavy with selling interest near 119.70 yen and above during the Asian session.

"The dollar took a breather after the recent dive. Officials have said the recent moves in currencies reflect the penetration of the agreement by the Group of Seven (G7), and that seems to be true," a city bank dealer said.

Comments by the head of business lobby Keidanren, who is also chairman of Toyota Motor Corp, that an exchange rate of 110 to 120 yen per dollar was appropriate for Toyota Motor's operations, also weighed on the greenback, some dealers said.
But dealers said the dollar was unlikely to fall sharply due to short-covering interest by those who had sold the dollar heavily during its recent nosedive.
Some importer bids were also seen supporting the dollar near 119 yen in afternoon trade, while Japanese investors were said to be sidelined, dealers added.
In dollar/mark trade, the dollar faced strong resistance at around 1.7070/75, a dealer at European bank in Singapore said.

In cross trade, the mark hovered near 70 yen during Asian trading hours after falling as low as around 69.64 yen. Trade was sandwiched between profit-taking sales on the upside and short-covering on dips.
